Trial #1: New plan: 

In my previous attempt, I correctly calculated the average treatment effect (ATE) to assess the effect of smoking on college admission. However, I failed to consider the joint distribution of smoking status and effort correctly. Specifically, I used the probabilities of being hard-working and lazy for smokers and nonsmokers separately, but I should have used the law of total probability to calculate the joint probabilities of smoking status and effort.

To correct this, I will recalculate the joint probabilities of smoking status and effort using the law of total probability. For example, the probability of being hard-working and smoking can be calculated as follows:

P(H|S) = P(H|S=1)P(S=1) + P(H|S=0)P(S=0)
= 61% * 61% + 40% * 39%
= 0.61 * 0.61 + 0.40 * 0.39
= 0.3711 + 0.156
= 0.5271

Similarly, I will recalculate the joint probabilities of smoking status and effort for being lazy and smoking, and for being hard-working and not smoking. Then, I will use these joint probabilities to calculate the probabilities of college admission for smokers and nonsmokers, and finally, I will calculate the ATE to assess the effect of smoking on college admission.
